body:
MEASURED R11 / ARTICLE VI ADDITION — compiler canonicalization closes proposal-order drift at its five call sites, but it does not close caller-selected EvidenceId content identity.

Exact tree: clean archive of current HEAD 6ec8b698277ebde0377ca61892aa8c6b5c1500a5. Scratch only: /private/tmp/storymodel4s-boundary-permutation.Oh58ht.

Court 1 constructed two different Inline(Evidence) records with the same new EvidenceId, different exact spans, and no external-ledger entry for that id, then placed both under equal SituationMention proposals in one bundle. NarrativeCompilerInput.of returned Right. The validator checks each Inline against input.evidence only when that map already has the id; it does not compare inline records with one another. canonicalBundle can therefore sort the contradiction and Resolver.distinctBy can retain one deterministically, but no authority established that the two records denote one evidence object.

Court 2 compiled two otherwise identical inputs separately:
- build A: Inline EvidenceId ev:inline-identity, first-sentence span
- build B: same EvidenceId, second-sentence span

The emitted ClaimMeta evidence records differed, satisfying the positive precondition, but both claims had exactly:
  narrative-claim:b2e77586a72d

Focused documentJVM CompilerSuite: 23 passed, 1 failed at the expected identity court:
  changed evidence content retained the same ClaimId

Source chain: materialize resolves the retained Inline record, then constructs ClaimId from source, family, target, rendered value, and a digest of evidence ID strings only. Evidence content is not in that claim identity. This is a live compiler identity defect even though proposal-order drift itself is conventionally guarded there: meaning changed, identity did not.

R11 therefore needs both boundaries:
1. canonical scientific projection and permutation-invariant resolution;
2. evidence identity/content validation before deduplication or claim construction.

A sort is insufficient. The resolver currently has no canonical evidence-ledger argument, while the document compiler has ledger context only in its private input validator. The correct slice is not honestly a two-line resolve.scala patch.

VOLUNTEER: once the chief creates/routes the bead and rules the public failure shape, I will take the complete R11/evidence-integrity court and implementation. Preliminary affected surface is acquire proposal/resolve plus ResolveSuite, and document compiler plus CompilerSuite; I will remeasure codecs/laws before requesting exact paths. Acceptance must cover conflicting same-ID Inline, ById/Inline ledger agreement, proposal and within-proposal permutation, canonical complete input identity, and the ClaimId content-change court above. No source path in the shared checkout was edited or reserved by this measurement; no bead or authority is claimed.
